title: Heterogeneous Computing Pipeline for Stream Compression
description: Authored a custom OpenCL compute kernel on a Xilinx Ultra96 FPGA with a C++ host runtime managing host-to-device DMA transfers, kernel dispatch, and memory coherency — achieving 135 Mbps per-thread throughput, horizontally scalable by cores and FPGA synthesis real estate.
highlights: Authored a custom OpenCL compute kernel for stream compression on the Xilinx Ultra96 platform
Built a C++ host runtime managing host-to-device DMA transfers, kernel dispatch scheduling, and memory coherency
Profiled kernel occupancy, memory bandwidth, and host-device transfer overhead; applied tiling and buffer reuse to maximize accelerator efficiency
Content-defined chunking (Gear hash table) with NEON-accelerated SHA-256 on CPU for horizontal scaling
Achieved 135 Mbps per-thread throughput — limited only by number of cores and kernel synthesis real estate; validated against NumPy reference results

title: Autonomous F1/10th Robot Racer Agent — High Performance
description: Full-stack autonomous racing system on the F1Tenth platform with LiDAR, depth camera, and IMU on an NVIDIA Jetson via ROS2. Implemented Particle Filter SLAM for 6-DOF localization and GPU-accelerated MPPI trajectory sampling for control at 50 Hz. Placed 2nd in University Competition.
highlights: Team lead managing 4 students; deployed a fully autonomous ground vehicle on NVIDIA Jetson integrating LiDAR, depth camera, and IMU via ROS2 on Ubuntu Linux
Implemented Particle Filter SLAM for real-time 6-DOF pose estimation at 50 Hz, fusing LiDAR point cloud, depth, and IMU streams
Integrated GPU-accelerated sampling-based MPPI (CUDA / JAX-XLA kernel fusion) evaluating 1000+ trajectory candidates per cycle for steering and throttle
Developed a Visual-Inertial Odometry pipeline using LoFTR transformer-based dense feature extraction for robust localization under varying lighting and texture
Built kinematic models, curvature controllers, Kalman/Markovian estimation, and safety-critical multithreaded ROS2 nodes — 2nd Rank University Competition

title: Optical Flow and Scene Reconstruction
description: Improved ego-motion tracking accuracy by 7% by implementing Lucas-Kanade optical flow with RANSAC outlier rejection for robust visual localization, integrating transformer-based (LoFTR) dense feature extraction for monocular 3D scene reconstruction.
highlights: Implemented Lucas-Kanade optical flow with RANSAC outlier rejection for robust ego-motion tracking
Improved scene recovery and ego-motion accuracy by 7% under challenging lighting and texture conditions
Integrated transformer-based (LoFTR) feature extraction for dense multi-view visual correspondence
Enabled monocular 3D scene reconstruction and mapping from image sequences

title: Agentic AI Manager — Cross-Model Communication & Scaling (Akka)
description: Built an Akka Actor system on Scala Play for multimodal scale-up and inter-model communication, improving resource utilization by 40% and cutting P99 message latency by 150 ms with an intelligent agent selector and load balancer. LightBend Akka challenge 2025.
highlights: Improved system resource utilization by 40% and reduced P99 message latency by 150 ms with a scalable Actor system manager on Scala Play
Enforced at-most-once and at-least-once delivery semantics per workload priority tier
Designed an intelligent agent selector and load balancer with asynchronous, queue-backed communication protocols routing cross-model workloads
Each agent runs on its own Akka actor — demonstrating functional programming for modular, cyber-intelligent automation frameworks

title: RISC-V Microprocessor on Lattice FPGA
description: Built a RISC-V ISA-compliant microprocessor with multicycle, 5-stage pipelining, and a custom 8-stage Divider Module at University of Pennsylvania. Achieved 17.65 MHz clock speed with AXI4-Lite cache.
highlights: RISC-V ISA-compliant microprocessor with multicycle and 5-stage pipelining
Custom 8-stage Divider Module for optimizing DIV instructions
Achieved 17.65 MHz clock speed with a 4-stage AXI4-Lite cache hierarchy
Synthesized and deployed on Lattice FPGA via Xilinx Vivado; validated with the Dhrystone benchmark suite under CocoTb simulation

title: Low-Light Image Enhancement using Transformer-Based Neural Network
description: Based on RetinexFormer, a transformer-based model with a modified loss criterion achieving PSNR 22.7 and live video enhancement at 5 FPS. Further accelerated via quantization, pruning, and GPU acceleration.
highlights: Trained a RetinexFormer transformer model based on Retinex theory for low-light image and video enhancement
Achieved PSNR of 22.7 with live video processing at 5 FPS
Experimented with Charbonnier Loss, L1-Luminance Loss, Gradient Graph Laplacian Regularizer, ReduceLROnPlateau scheduler, and Lion optimizer — cutting convergence time by 1.5%
Applied quantization, pruning, and vertical GPU acceleration to meet the real-time FPS target; visualized training dynamics with TensorBoard

title: DNN Compression, Quantization & GPU Inference Profiling
description: Achieved a 75% reduction in VGG16 memory footprint (500 MB to 125 MB) via INT8 quantization and structured pruning, with per-operator inference profiling across CUDA, Apple MPS, and CPU execution providers using ONNX Runtime.
highlights: Achieved 75% memory-footprint reduction on VGG16 (500 MB to 125 MB) via INT8 quantization and structured pruning while preserving inference accuracy
Developed a custom sparse Linear layer for iterative pruning and saved the compressed model in CSR format; experimented with Global, Channel, Structured, and Unstructured pruning
Lowered the PyTorch computational graph to an ONNX intermediate representation for framework-agnostic deployment
Profiled inference across CUDA, Apple MPS, and CPU execution providers via ONNX Runtime — identifying bandwidth-bound vs. compute-bound operators and quantifying numerical accuracy degradation

title: NSC Portfolio
description: A personal portfolio website built with React and Vite to showcase research, projects, and experience. Features dynamic JSON-driven content, media embeddings, and a responsive dark-theme design.
highlights: JSON-driven dynamic content — swap data without touching components
Video and photo media per item
Responsive dark-theme design
Resume download and social links
